text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended slightly lower in quiet trade. Business was dominated by August which lost $0.10 to close at $319.0 per tonne, while October gave up $1.20 to close at $314.30 per tonne. The market was in a pre-expiry mood, with a high proportion of AA trades in the volume and trades rolling positions from August into October playing a big role.

Raw sugar futures in New York closed a thinly traded session mostly unchanged. There was no fresh news to influence prices. Without fresh fundamental developments, prices are likely to remain within their current tight trading range. October and March closed unchanged at 11.06 and 11.21 cents/lb respectively. FUNDAMENTALS

EUROPE - The sugar beet areas in Western Europe remained mainly dry during the week ended July 8, which was of importance after recent heavy rains. Current indications are that a good crop is in prospect and that production may eventually turn out to be higher than was believed at the beginning of the season.

In Eastern Europe some beet areas are becoming too wet due to heavy rainfall over the past week. The problems are mainly in the Czech Republic where heavy floods will result in large agricultural losses. However, it is too early to estimate the full extent of the damage. Thousands of people had been forced to leave their homes, many houses were swept away by flood streams and 18 people are feared dead. Conditions are much better in Hungary and Romania.

In the former Soviet Union sugar beet areas reported moderate rainfall. Soil moisture is adequate for beet growth. However, the disappointing acreage figure in the Russian Federation is lowering production potential, but yield prospects are apparently good. According to the Rossakhsvyokla Sugar Beet Producers' Association, as reported by Reuters, beet weight on July 1 reached 151 grams compared to 132 grams the same date last year.

The number of beets per ha was put at 73,000 compared to 70,000 in 1996. This points to a beet weight of 11 tonnes per ha compared to 9.2 tonnes the same date last year. However, the figures for last year are not consistent with what was published in 1996.

UKRAINE - Sugar exports in April 1997 amounted to 122,294 tonnes, raw value, up from 105,870 tonnes the previous month. This brought cumulative exports in the first four months of 1997 (January/April) up to 372,403 tonnes. Major countries of destination in January/April 1997 were Russia with 251,200 tonnes whites, Belarus with 20,700 tonnes, Turkmenistan with 16,401 tonnes and Aserbaijan with 13,000 tonnes. Ukraine's sugar exports in 1997/98 are expected to fall because of a lower domestic output and increasing trade barriers in its main outlets.

GERMANY - Sugar imports in March 1997 amounted to 10,559 tonnes, raw value, up from 9,146 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first half of 1996/97 (October/March) up to 111,888 tonnes compared to 101,525 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 206,911 tonnes compared to 225,848 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were France with 77,796 tonnes whites against 74,556 tonnes and the Netherlands with 12,689 tonnes, up from 8,033 tonnes.

Sugar exports in March 1997 amounted to 119,793 tonnes, up from 89,431 tonnes in March 1996. This brought cumulative exports in the first half of 1996/97 up to 883,485 tonnes compared to 877,788 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 1.316 million tonnes, down from 1.452 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Italy with 117,873 tonnes whites against 42,801 tonnes, Belgium-Luxembourg with 110,523 tonnes compared to 104,486 tonnes, the United Arab Emirates with 100,450 tonnes compared to 105,305 tonnes and Switzerland with 51,790 tonnes, down from 56,068 tonnes.

DENMARK - There was only little rain in the week ended July 6 with temperatures staying above the long term mean. Precipitation levels since April 1 ranged between 130-183 mm compared to an average of 143-151 mm. Growth continues to be very good. Some regions report attacks by green and black aphids. Production prospects continue to be normal.
